name: Create a stock item once, with the unit it is counted in and the level at which it must be bought again
priorityReason: Requests, receipts, issues and counts all read the item. Nothing in the module works until it exists.

goal.capability: to define each stock item once, with its unit and its reorder level
goal.outcome: everything counted, requested, received and issued is counted in the same unit against the same item

secondaryActors.involvement: Receives, issues and counts against the items. Does not create them.

additional.description: An item falls below its reorder level, which offers it for inclusion in a stock request.

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin.
The category list exists, or the category is created as the item is.

postConditions: The item exists once, with its name, category, unit, reorder level and whether it is consumable or returnable.
The unit is fixed, so everything requested, received, issued and counted for that item is counted the same way.
The reorder level is set by the School Admin, not by whoever holds the store, since it commits the school to buying.
Whether the item is consumable or returnable is recorded, which decides whether an issue stays outstanding against the person who took it.
The item is available for requests, receipts, issues and counts.
Every change to the item is recorded with who made it.
Nothing was deleted. An item no longer stocked is deactivated and stays readable, since receipts, issues and counts reference it.

dataFields.name: Name
dataFields.validation: 2 to 100 characters. Unique within its category (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Category
dataFields.validation: What kind of item it is. Lists and counts group by it.

dataFields.name: Unit
dataFields.validation: The unit the item is counted in. Fixed once set, since a change would make every past count mean something different (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Reorder level
dataFields.validation: The quantity at which the item must be bought again. Zero or more. Set by the School Admin because it commits the school to buying (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Consumable or returnable
dataFields.validation: A consumable is used up once issued. A return is expected back and stays outstanding against the person who took it (BR-4).

dataFields.name: On hand
dataFields.validation: The quantity currently held, from receipts, issues and counts. Never typed here (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Below reorder level
dataFields.validation: Set where the quantity on hand has fallen to or below the reorder level, which offers it for a request (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Deactivation reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Required to deactivate an item (BR-9).
dataFields.example: The school has moved to refillable markers.

businessRules.rule: An item is created once, and everything in the module works against it. Two items for the same thing is two stock balances for one shelf.
The unit is fixed once the item is in use. Changing it would make every past receipt, issue and count mean something different from what it meant when it was recorded.
A reorder level is a standing commitment to buy rather than a description, so it is set by the School Admin and not by whoever happens to hold the store.

An item is consumable or returnable, and the difference matters. A consumable is used up once issued — a marker, a ream of paper, a reagent. A return is expected back — a projector remote, a set of keys, a lab instrument — and stays outstanding against the person who took it until it is returned.
The quantity on hand is never typed here. It comes from receipts, issues and counts, and this screen shows it rather than setting it.
An item name is unique within its category. Two entries called the same thing in the same category is how a store ends up with two balances for one shelf.
An item at or below its reorder level is flagged, and is offered for inclusion when a stock request is raised.
Every change to an item is recorded with who made it. A reorder level that moved without explanation is a purchasing decision nobody made.
An item is deactivated rather than deleted, with a reason, and stays readable. Receipts, issues and counts reference it, and deleting it would leave a past count unreadable.
A deactivated item cannot be requested, received or issued, but its history stays and it still appears in a count of what is physically on the shelf until the shelf is clear.

transitions.condition: The quantity on hand falls to or below the reorder level (BR-7).
A receipt takes the quantity back above the level.
Deactivated with a reason. The history stays (BR-9).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inventory → Stock items → Create an item
basicFlow.userAction: Creates the item with its name, category, the unit it is counted in, the reorder level, and whether it is consumable or returnable.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the name is unique within the category and requires all five.

basicFlow.userAction: Selects the unit the item will be counted in.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Fixes the unit once the item is in use, since changing it would make every past count mean something different.

basicFlow.userAction: Sets the level at which the item must be bought again.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records it against the item. Only the School Admin may set it.

basicFlow.navigation: Create an item → Consumable or returnable
basicFlow.userAction: Records whether the item is used up once issued or is expected back.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Decides whether an issue of this item stays outstanding against the person who took it.
Makes the item available for requests, receipts, issues and counts, showing the quantity on hand rather than setting it.
Flags the item when the quantity on hand falls to or below the reorder level, and offers it for inclusion in a request.

basicFlow.userAction: Changes the item as circumstances change.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the change with who made it, and refuses a change to the unit once the item is in use.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
